\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جام} (jām)}{جام (jām)}]{\ur{جام} (jām) — a traffic jam}

\label{lesson:UR-C393-jam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to stroll, then the Urdu for to pant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جام}}
\textbf{\ur{جام}} — \emph{jām} — \textquotedblleft{}a traffic jam\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پل} \ur{پر} \ur{بڑا} \ur{جام} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pul par baṛā jām thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a huge traffic jam on the bridge.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جام}} (\emph{jām}) is borrowed from English \emph{jam}, as in a traffic jam.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jām}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jām}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pul par baṛā jām thā.} — There was a huge traffic jam on the bridge.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to stroll, then the Urdu for to pant, then say \emph{jām} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{جام} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A traffic jam\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہارن} (hārn)}{ہارن (hārn)}]{\ur{ہارن} (hārn) — a horn (of a vehicle)}

\label{lesson:UR-C393-harn}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to pant, then the Urdu for a traffic jam.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہارن}}
\textbf{\ur{ہارن}} — \emph{hārn} — \textquotedblleft{}a horn (of a vehicle)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{جام} \ur{میں} \ur{سب} \ur{لوگ} \ur{ہارن} \ur{بجاتے} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jām meṅ sab log hārn bajāte haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In a jam everyone sounds the horn.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہارن}} (\emph{hārn}) is borrowed from English \emph{horn}; you sound it with \textbf{\ur{بجانا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کنڈکٹر} (kanḍakṭar)}{کنڈکٹر (kanḍakṭar)}]{\ur{کنڈکٹر} (kanḍakṭar) — a conductor (on a bus)}

Before the new one: say the Urdu for a traffic jam, then the Urdu for a horn (of a vehicle).

\textbf{\ur{کنڈکٹر}} (\emph{kanḍakṭar}) is borrowed from English \emph{conductor}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سرکنا} (saraknā)}{سرکنا (saraknā)}]{\ur{سرکنا} (saraknā) — to edge forward; to slide}

\label{lesson:UR-C393-sarakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a horn (of a vehicle), then the Urdu for a conductor (on a bus).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سرکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سرکنا}} — \emph{saraknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to edge forward; to slide\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{جام} \ur{میں} \ur{گاڑیاں} \ur{آہستہ} \ur{آہستہ} \ur{سرکتی} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jām meṅ gāṛiyāṅ āhistā āhistā saraktī haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In a jam the cars inch forward.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{بس} \ur{آگے} \ur{سرکی}, \emph{voh bas āge sarkī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سرکنا}} (\emph{saraknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{saraknā} under Sanskrit \emph{sarati}, \textquotedblleft{}runs, glides\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13250); \textbf{\ur{سرکانا}} is the form for moving something else.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saraknā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saraknā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jām meṅ gāṛiyāṅ āhistā āhistā saraktī haiṅ.} — In a jam the cars inch forward.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a horn (of a vehicle), then the Urdu for a conductor (on a bus), then say \emph{saraknā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{سرکنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To edge forward; to slide\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رکوانا} (rukvānā)}{رکوانا (rukvānā)}]{\ur{رکوانا} (rukvānā) — to have (something) stopped}

\label{lesson:UR-C393-rukvana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a conductor (on a bus), then the Urdu for to edge forward.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رکوانا}}
\textbf{\ur{رکوانا}} — \emph{rukvānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to have (something) stopped\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کنڈکٹر} \ur{نے} \ur{اسٹاپ} \ur{پر} \ur{بس} \ur{رکوائی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kanḍakṭar ne isṭāp par bas rukvāī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The conductor got the bus to stop at the stop.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{گاڑی} \ur{رکوائی}, \emph{us ne gāṛī rukvāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رکوانا}} (\emph{rukvānā}) is built on \textbf{\ur{رکنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to stop\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-vā-} that means getting someone else to do it; CDIAL lists the partner verb, Hindi \emph{roknā}, under \emph{rōkk}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 10827).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rukvānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rukvānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kanḍakṭar ne isṭāp par bas rukvāī.} — The conductor got the bus to stop at the stop.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a conductor (on a bus), then the Urdu for to edge forward, then say \emph{rukvānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{رکوانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To have (something) stopped\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Engines and Carriages to Traffic Jams}

\label{lesson:UR-R393-review-386-393}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for an engine and a compartment (of a train).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an engine, a compartment (of a train), a railway line, a whistle, to sound
  \item a porter, a trunk, to load, to haul, to seat (someone)
  \item a signal (for trains or traffic), a railway junction, a gate, a berth (on a train), to gaze (at)
  \item on board, a bundle (tied in cloth), to slide (something) along, a yawn, to doze
  \item an arrival, setting off, lateness, cancelled, to take down
  \item a booking, a queue, a counter, a rush (of people), to push in
  \item a stand (for taxis or rickshaws), a bus stop, a path, to stroll, to pant
  \item a traffic jam, a horn (of a vehicle), a conductor (on a bus), to edge forward, to have (something) stopped
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An engine? (\textbf{\ur{انجن}}, \emph{injan}.) A compartment (of a train)? (\textbf{\ur{ڈبہ}}, \emph{ḍabbā}.) A railway line? (\textbf{\ur{لائن}}, \emph{lāin}.) A whistle? (\textbf{\ur{سیٹی}}, \emph{sīṭī}.) To sound? (\textbf{\ur{بجنا}}, \emph{bajnā}.) A porter? (\textbf{\ur{قلی}}, \emph{qulī}.) A trunk? (\textbf{\ur{صندوق}}, \emph{sandūq}.) To load? (\textbf{\ur{لادنا}}, \emph{lādnā}.) To haul? (\textbf{\ur{ڈھونا}}, \emph{ḍhonā}.) To seat (someone)? (\textbf{\ur{بٹھانا}}, \emph{biṭhānā}.) A signal (for trains or traffic)? (\textbf{\ur{سگنل}}, \emph{signal}.) A railway junction? (\textbf{\ur{جنکشن}}, \emph{jankshan}.) A gate? (\textbf{\ur{پھاٹک}}, \emph{phāṭak}.) A berth (on a train)? (\textbf{\ur{برتھ}}, \emph{barth}.) To gaze (at)? (\textbf{\ur{تاکنا}}, \emph{tāknā}.) On board? (\textbf{\ur{سوار}}, \emph{savār}.) A bundle (tied in cloth)? (\textbf{\ur{گٹھری}}, \emph{gaṭhrī}.) To slide (something) along? (\textbf{\ur{سرکانا}}, \emph{sarkānā}.) A yawn? (\textbf{\ur{جماہی}}, \emph{jamāhī}.) To doze? (\textbf{\ur{اونگھنا}}, \emph{ūṅghnā}.) An arrival? (\textbf{\ur{آمد}}, \emph{āmad}.) Setting off? (\textbf{\ur{روانہ}}, \emph{ravānā}.) Lateness? (\textbf{\ur{تاخیر}}, \emph{tākhīr}.) Cancelled? (\textbf{\ur{منسوخ}}, \emph{mansūkh}.) To take down? (\textbf{\ur{اتارنا}}, \emph{utārnā}.) A booking? (\textbf{\ur{بکنگ}}, \emph{buking}.) A queue? (\textbf{\ur{قطار}}, \emph{qatār}.) A counter? (\textbf{\ur{کاؤنٹر}}, \emph{kāunṭar}.) A rush (of people)? (\textbf{\ur{رش}}, \emph{rash}.) To push in? (\textbf{\ur{گھسنا}}, \emph{ghusnā}.) A stand (for taxis or rickshaws)? (\textbf{\ur{اسٹینڈ}}, \emph{isṭainḍ}.) A bus stop? (\textbf{\ur{اسٹاپ}}, \emph{isṭāp}.) A path? (\textbf{\ur{راہ}}, \emph{rāh}.) To stroll? (\textbf{\ur{ٹہلنا}}, \emph{ṭahalnā}.) To pant? (\textbf{\ur{ہانپنا}}, \emph{hāṅpnā}.) A traffic jam? (\textbf{\ur{جام}}, \emph{jām}.) A horn (of a vehicle)? (\textbf{\ur{ہارن}}, \emph{hārn}.) A conductor (on a bus)? (\textbf{\ur{کنڈکٹر}}, \emph{kanḍakṭar}.) To edge forward? (\textbf{\ur{سرکنا}}, \emph{saraknā}.) To have (something) stopped? (\textbf{\ur{رکوانا}}, \emph{rukvānā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
